newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge in late trade Thursday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds surge in late trade Thursday.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities bounced back from earlier doldrums after a healthy Treasury auction Thursday induced a buying spree, traders said.
Earlier in the day, pass-throughs were pulled lower as the the 6-3/4 percent 30-year benchmark Treasury bond was quoted off 21/32, yielding 6.67 percent, the highest level since October 29.
However the Treasury's auction of $10 billion in 30-year bonds, the last leg of a $38.5 billion quarterly refunding effort, drew better-than-expected bids later in the day, said one regional trader.
"The Treasury auction gave us a rally as well," he said, explaining that the volatility in the Treasury market spurred a rally in mortgage-backed securities.
"If we can bounce around instead of keeping in the (6.50 percent to 7.50 percent) range, in either direction, people get excited," he said.
By late afternoon Thursday, pass-throughs were 2/32 to 15/32 higher. Spreads over Treasuries narrowed.
Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 13/32 at 100-31/32 to yield 106 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac paper were both 14/32 higher at 100-28/32 and 101-01/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was up 11/32 at 101-25/32 to yield 6.26 percent.
